Scene: a close view at table height: the patient's forearm and open hand rest palm-up on a folded white towel; the practitioner holds a small white handheld low-level laser probe held just above the crease of the wrist, casting a small red glow on the skin. Over the patient's body, a luminous augmented-reality anatomy overlay: the wrist and hand bones and the median nerve passing through the carpal tunnel, drawn in delicate glowing teal engraving lines exactly where they sit under the skin, crisp and anatomically precise, like a living anatomical plate. The painful area glows with a soft, diffuse red-orange warmth inside the body at the carpal tunnel at the base of the palm, subtle, like inflamed tissue seen through the skin, and the treatment is focused precisely on that red area. The practitioner is a man in a crisp white dress shirt with the sleeves rolled to the forearm and dark trousers, framed from the chest down so his head and face are out of the frame. The patient is a woman in her forties; only her forearm and open hand are in frame; the patient's face may be seen, relaxed, eyes closed or looking away. Hands: every hand anatomically perfect, five fingers each with natural joints and nails, a natural grip, no fused, extra or missing fingers. Every body complete and continuous. No text, logos, labels or readable screens.
